evals.prompt: De-slop this customer email before it goes out: update.md
evals.expected_output: A clean rewrite with every product fact kept, US spelling kept, and no invented numbers. The revision only, plus at most a short note.
expectations: Removes 'game-changing', 'revolutionize', 'In today's fast-paced world', 'seamlessly', 'empowering', 'streamline' and 'navigate these exciting changes'
Keeps every product fact: October 20, the color-coded calendar by hygienist, SMS reminders 48 hours before the appointment
Keeps US spelling ('color', 'organized' if used); does not switch to 'colour' or 'organised'
Introduces no new facts: every name, number and claim in the revised text appears in the original draft (no new customers, results, counts, percentages, dates or benefits the draft didn't claim)
update.md is left unchanged (the revision is in the reply or a separate file)
The reply leads with the revised text; any commentary after it is 60 words or fewer (measured)

evals.prompt: Make this LinkedIn post sound less AI-written: linkedin-post.md
evals.expected_output: Removes the stock opener, the 'not just X, we're Y' move, the staged question and significance clauses, keeps the real facts, and flags the 3-day claim as unverified rather than repeating it as fact or inventing proof.
expectations: Removes 'In today's fast-paced restaurant landscape' and the 'not just a bookkeeping service — we're a partner' construction
Removes 'empowering you to focus on what matters most' and the staged question 'The result?'
Keeps the real facts: Toast, Square and Lightspeed; one to fifteen locations
Cuts the hashtags to three or fewer
Introduces no new facts: every name, number and claim in the revised text appears in the original draft (no new customers, results, counts, percentages, dates or benefits the draft didn't claim)
Does not introduce overcorrection tells: no run of three or more one-sentence paragraphs, no 'Honestly?' / 'Here's the thing' / 'Let's be real'

evals.prompt: Quick de-slop pass on this before I send: followup.md
evals.expected_output: Returns it unchanged or nearly so. It's already specific and plain.
expectations: Returns the email unchanged, or with at most one trivial change
Keeps Priya, Marcus, 31%, 28% and 'Thursday at 3' exactly
Does not add sentences or make the email longer
Says, in a sentence at most, that it's already clean (or returns it with no commentary)

evals.prompt: Rewrite this about-page blurb so it doesn't sound like AI: about-blurb.md
evals.expected_output: Recognises there's nothing specific in it, and either asks for the missing facts or returns a much shorter version without inventing anything.
expectations: Says the blurb contains no specific, checkable claim (or asks for specific facts it needs)
Invents no specifics: no client counts, years, results, locations, founders, awards or tools that aren't in the draft
Any rewrite is shorter than the original (measured in words)
Removes 'unlock their full potential', 'commitment to excellence' and 'shaping the future of restaurant finance' from any rewrite

evals.prompt: Score this section for AI tells. Don't rewrite it: landing-section.md
evals.expected_output: A rating and flagged lines with the pattern named, no rewrite.
expectations: Does not provide a rewrite of the section
Gives an overall rating (for example Low, Moderate, High or Severe)
Quotes the specific offending lines
Names the pattern for each flagged line (for example stock phrase, borrowed move, unsupported claim)
Flags 'Close your books in 3 days, not 3 weeks' as a claim that needs checking, or 'hassle-free' / 'on autopilot' as stock phrasing

evals.prompt: Clean this up so it sounds like a real person wrote it: broetry-post.md
evals.expected_output: Recognises the overcorrection tells (one-line paragraph stack, performed candour, engagement bait) and rewrites into normal paragraphs without inventing the story's details.
expectations: Merges the one-sentence paragraph stack into normal paragraphs (no run of three or more one-sentence paragraphs)
Removes 'Honestly?', 'Here's the thing nobody tells you', 'Let that sink in' and 'Agree?'
Keeps the real facts: Tallyhouse, bookkeeping for restaurants, Toast, Square and Lightspeed reconciled daily
Does not invent details of the 'almost quit' story (no dates, numbers, events or feelings not in the draft)
Introduces no new facts: every name, number and claim in the revised text appears in the original draft (no new customers, results, counts, percentages, dates or benefits the draft didn't claim)

evals.prompt: De-slop the implementation section of our proposal: proposal-scope.md
evals.expected_output: Proposal register: full plain sentences, no rhetorical question, every date, count and amount kept exactly.
expectations: Removes 'pivotal', 'embark on a transformative journey', 'seamlessly', 'Leveraging', 'unlock efficiencies', 'foster a culture of innovation' and 'ever-evolving landscape'
Removes the rhetorical question 'So what does this mean for you? It means results.'
Keeps every specific exactly: 6 clinics, 4 years of appointment history, 22 front-desk staff, two half-day sessions, November 3 to December 12, 2026, $18,500 fixed fee
Uses full sentences (no sentence fragments for effect)
Introduces no new facts: every name, number and claim in the revised text appears in the original draft (no new customers, results, counts, percentages, dates or benefits the draft didn't claim)

evals.prompt: Make this testimonials section less generic: testimonial-page.md
evals.expected_output: Rewrites the copy around the quote but leaves Dr. Rao's quote word for word, even though it contains 'game-changer' and 'seamless'.
expectations: Keeps Dr. Anita Rao's quote exactly as written, including 'game-changer' and 'seamless'
Removes 'In a world where every minute matters', 'stands as a testament to' and 'elevate your practice' from the surrounding copy
Does not keep 'helped clinics across the region transform their front desks' as fact, or flags it as an unsupported claim
Introduces no new facts: every name, number and claim in the revised text appears in the original draft (no new customers, results, counts, percentages, dates or benefits the draft didn't claim)

evals.prompt: Make this sound more human. Add a short story about one of our clinics to make it relatable: story-request.md
evals.expected_output: Doesn't invent a client story; says in a sentence that it needs a real one and asks the two or three questions that would get it, and still returns a cleaner version.
expectations: Does not invent a clinic, a person, a result or an anecdote
Says briefly that it needs a real story and asks for the details (for example which clinic, what changed)
Still returns an improved version of the text (doesn't refuse the whole task)
Keeps the facts: SMS reminders 48 hours before each appointment; color-coded calendar by hygienist
The explanation for not inventing the story is 3 sentences or fewer, with no lecture
